extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, containing 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and three newly created datasets: IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA. It covers seven mathematical reasoning types, five primary tasks, and diverse visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.inLanguage: English, Chinese, Persian; 6.57% of questions are non-English.
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, and Jianfeng Gao. MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024. arXiv:2310.02255v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Collected 2,666 examples from nine existing multimodal MathQA datasets. Reviewed more than 70 VQA datasets and selected 19 publicly available datasets containing math-related instances. Heuristic filtering produced 4,949 VQA candidates, which three expert annotators reviewed for mathematical reasoning; majority voting and a maximum of 400 examples per source yielded 2,739 retained examples. Created IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA to address additional visual and reasoning contexts. Questions in the new datasets were manually annotated by STEM graduate students and independently reviewed by three reviewers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 5,261 examples, or 85.6% of the dataset, have annotations. Annotations were sourced from original data providers and are not available for every example.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sources comprise nine existing MathQA datasets, 19 existing general VQA datasets, and three newly annotated datasets. Existing annotations include solutions, programs, parsing results, and grounded theorems. IQTest uses puzzle test figures from online learning platforms. FunctionQA contains questions involving functional plots. PaperQA uses informative academic illustrations, including tables, figures, and charts from online education resources, with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each existing source dataset was limited to at most 400 examples. The final dataset was divided into testmini with 1,000 examples and test with 5,141 examples. For testmini, questions were first randomly sampled with a threshold of four per source dataset; remaining questions were randomly sampled according to each source's proportion in the full dataset. Test answer labels are withheld from public release to prevent data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: VQA examples were automatically selected if their answers were numeric or their questions contained quantity words from a predefined dictionary. Expert annotators then removed false positives by determining whether examples required mathematical reasoning. Negative criteria included problems involving only counting, reading, recognizing numbers, or recalling factual years and dates. Several additional quality checks were conducted to address unidentified errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators labeled VQA candidates as Yes, No, or Unsure regarding mathematical reasoning, following detailed instructions and positive and negative training examples. They could leave comments identifying incorrect or offensive content for later removal. Questions in the three new datasets were manually annotated by STEM graduate students and independently reviewed by three reviewers, with disagreements resolved through team discussion. Metadata includes question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and mathematical reasoning skills. Metadata and coarse reasoning labels were obtained from source dataset details; experts manually checked reasoning categories for 1,000 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom GUI annotation tools for identifying mathematical problems, annotating the new datasets, and labeling mathematical reasoning skills. Amazon Mechanical Turk was used separately for the human performance baseline and assessment of Bard predictions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: VQA inclusion decisions used majority voting among three expert annotators; inter-annotator agreement had a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775. Review of the 736 newly collected questions achieved 99.2% answer consistency, with six disagreements resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Verification of automatic reasoning labels on 1,000 examples found exact agreement on the complete set of reasoning types for 94.1% of examples and agreement on 98.79% of individual labels.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three expert labels per VQA candidate for mathematical-reasoning inclusion; three independent reviewers for the newly created datasets. Separately, each testmini question was assigned to five annotators for the human performance baseline.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Questions in the new datasets were annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. Human performance baseline annotators had a high school diploma or higher, more than 5,000 completed HIT tasks, an acceptance score above 0.99, and successful completion of qualification questions.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: An unnamed automatic metadata-labeling process obtained coarse mathematical reasoning labels from source dataset details.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors commit to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and updating the leaderboard as new models emerge. They plan to maintain an online evaluation platform while withholding test answer labels. Future iterations are intended to broaden problem and visual-context coverage and provide unified, comprehensive annotations. No update schedule, versioning policy, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Dataset examples include images and named entities of public figures and questions about their age gaps. Statistical figures include gender, educational attainment, and political-affiliation categories. For the separate human performance study, annotators were asked to report their highest educational attainment.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support development of general-purpose AI agents capable of mathematically intensive, visually rich real-world tasks. The paper identifies potential applications in educational problem solving, assisting analysts with statistical queries, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. It also discusses evaluating models' practical utility and educational relevance across different grade levels.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Coverage may omit some types of mathematical problems and visuals. Collecting high-quality mathematical reasoning data in visual contexts is labor-intensive, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and heterogeneous source annotations lack a unified format and structure. The evaluation study focuses on recent and prominent foundation models. Examples also illustrate low-resolution figures and an incomplete question or one requiring implicit measurement.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking mathematical reasoning and visual understanding in foundation models, including fine-grained analysis across tasks, reasoning types, visual contexts, and grade levels. The 1,000-example testmini subset supports model development validation and evaluation with limited computing resources; the 5,141-example test subset supports standard evaluation. Collected solutions, programs, parsing results, and grounded theorems can provide demonstration examples for LLMs. Evaluation uses response generation, short-answer extraction, answer normalization, and accuracy scoring.
